statement_record.book: For a locally small C, a functor F : C^op -> Set and an object c, evaluation at the identity is a bijection Nat(C(-,c), F) ≅ F c, NATURAL IN BOTH c AND F; consequently every natural transformation C(-,c) => C(-,c') is postcomposition with a unique morphism c -> c'.
statement_record.intree: ∀ A : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] F ≅ F A, with to := fun x => transform[x] A id (setoid isomorphism in Sets); and ∀ A B : C, Presheaves [Hom ─,A] [Hom ─,B] ≊ A ~> B.

The file header (Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:22) claims 'natural in both A and F' in prose only; nothing downstream proves or uses a naturality square for the Yoneda bijection. The second clause (2.2.8) is fully present, in fact in a slightly stronger packaging (a Sets-isomorphism Yoneda_Embedding, plus separate Full/Faithful instances and the hom-set bijection Yoneda_Embedding' in Functor/Hom.v:109).

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem GAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (sols : forall d : D, SolutionSet U d) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.
Theorem GAFT_from_initials {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (H : forall d : D, @Initial (=(d) ↓ U)) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.

Definition SAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x : C, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U } := GAFT U comp cont (SAFT_solution_set U comp G WP cover).

statement_record.book: For U : A -> S continuous with A complete and both categories locally small, U has a left adjoint if ANY of: (i) every s/U has an initial object; (ii) the SOLUTION SET condition — for each s a SET of arrows f_i : s -> U a_i through which every f : s -> U a factors as U(k) ∘ f_i; (iii) A has a small coseparating set and every collection of subobjects of a fixed object has an intersection (wide pullback).
statement_record.intree: GAFT_from_initials (clause i, verbatim: initial object of =(d) ↓ U for every d, no other hypothesis needed); GAFT (clause ii, with `Record SolutionSet U d := { sol_index : Type; sol_obj; sol_arr : ∀ i, d ~> U (sol_obj i); sol_covers : ∀ {c} (h : d ~> U c), { i & { t & fmap[U] t ∘ sol_arr i ≈ h } } }`); SAFT (clause iii, but taking `SubobjectCover` — the factorization of every h through a well-powered subobject of the cogenerator product — as an ADDITIONAL DATA HYPOTHESIS).
statement_record.strength_comparison: Clauses (i) and (ii): same (arguably intree-stronger — GAFT_from_initials needs no completeness or continuity at all, and GAFT's continuity hypothesis is the cone-level PreservesImageLimit, which Construction/Comma/Limit.v:264 shows every right adjoint satisfies; local smallness is carried implicitly by universe polymorphism). Clause (iii): intree-weaker — SAFT's conclusion is only reached after ASSUMING SubobjectCover, i.e. exactly the step the book derives from the existence of intersections of subobjects.

gap: Clause (iii) (SAFT) is conditional on an assumed datum rather than derived from the book's hypotheses. Riehl's clause (iii) asks only for a small coseparating set plus intersections (wide pullbacks) of arbitrary families of subobjects; the in-tree SAFT instead requires, on top of Cogenerator and the well-poweredness datum SubobjectIndex, the hypothesis `SubobjectCover U comp G WP : ∀ d c (h : d ~> U c), { i & { s : d ~> U (sub_dom .. i) & { t & fmap[U] t ∘ s ≈ h } } }` — the image-factorization-through-a-subobject-of-the-cogenerator-product step, which is precisely what intersections are used to construct. Intersections / wide pullbacks of families of subobjects are not formalized anywhere in-tree, so clause (iii) as the book states it is not derivable in the library. Clauses (i) and (ii) are fully present.

statement_record.book: If U : A -> S has a left adjoint and creates coequalizers of U-split pairs (Beck-monadic) then: (i) U is conservative; (ii) U creates all limits existing in S; (iii) U creates all colimits existing in S that are preserved by the induced monad T and by T^2; (iv) if S is locally small, complete and cocomplete and U preserves filtered colimits then A has all small colimits.

statement_record.book: For K : C -> D with C small and D locally small, and any E: if E is COCOMPLETE the restriction K* : E^D -> E^C has a left adjoint Lan_K given by a colimit formula; if E is COMPLETE it has a right adjoint Ran_K given by the dual limit formula, so Lan_K ⊣ K* ⊣ Ran_K. Moreover, for K fully faithful, Lan_K ⊣ K* is coreflective and K* ⊣ Ran_K reflective (the Kan extensions restrict back to the original functor).
statement_record.intree: Induced : [B,C] ⟶ [A,C] := (− ◯ F) is the restriction functor; `Class LeftKan := { Lan : [A,C] ⟶ [B,C]; lan_adjoint : Lan ⊣ Induced }` and `Class RightKan := { Ran : [A,C] ⟶ [B,C]; ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran }` package exactly the adjoint characterization, and RightKan_to_LocalRightKan / LeftKan_to_LocalLeftKan derive the local (universal-transformation) forms from the global one.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the adjunctions Lan ⊣ K* and K* ⊣ Ran are the DEFINITION of the global Kan extensions (a hypothesis class), not a conclusion.
